title: FDA Drug Safety Communication: Low magnesium levels can be associated with long-term use of Proton Pump Inhibitor drugs (PPIs)
journal: US Food and Drug Administration, Drug Safety Communication, 2 March 2011
result: Review of 38 Adverse Event Reporting System cases and 23 published cases, at least 8 of them overlapping. Prescription PPIs may cause hypomagnesaemia when taken for prolonged periods, in most cases longer than one year; in about one quarter of cases magnesium supplementation alone was insufficient and the PPI was stopped. After stopping, magnesium normalised in a median of one week; after restarting, hypomagnesaemia recurred in a median of two weeks. Serious events included tetany, seizures, arrhythmias and hypocalcaemia with normal parathyroid hormone. The mechanism is unknown, possibly altered intestinal absorption. Serum magnesium should be considered before and periodically during prolonged treatment, especially with digoxin, loop or thiazide diuretics or other drugs causing hypomagnesaemia. Patients should not stop a prescription PPI without talking to their healthcare professional. Lists Dexilant (dexlansoprazole) among prescription PPIs.
